description: Settings for the crucible coding agent. Formats are unstable while the version is 0.x: any key here may be renamed or removed in any release, with no deprecation period.

compaction.description: What happens when the model's window fills up

askOnResume.description: How large a session has to be, in tokens, before picking it up asks whether to carry it whole. Zero never asks

keep.description: How many tokens of recent turns are kept word for word after the rest becomes a recap

recap.description: Maximum tokens a structured compaction recap may produce; ordinary recaps stop earlier

reserve.description: Tokens to keep free for the next answer and the tools it calls, instead of the room crucible works out from the model

spendCeiling.description: The most tokens one turn may produce before crucible stops it, where a runaway turn is worth bounding

when.description: Whether a full window is answered by compacting the session, or by letting the turn fail

env.description: Environment variables for the commands crucible runs. A file under the working directory may set only crucible's own CRUCIBLE_CODE_ names

CRUCIBLE_CODE_MOUSE_SCROLL_SPEED.description: How many rows of the transcript one notch of the wheel moves

config.description: Settings for the extension itself, in whatever names its own documentation gives. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

digest.description: The manifest digest this extension was agreed to at, as --extensions prints it. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

enabled.description: Whether crucible may run this extension. Not enough on its own: `digest` says which program was agreed to. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

extensions.description: Per-extension settings, keyed by the identifier the extension's manifest states

send.description: Which press sends a prompt: enter sends and Shift+Enter, Alt+Enter or Ctrl+J opens a line; altEnter swaps the two, for a terminal that keeps Enter for itself

mcp.description: MCP servers crucible may be asked to start

args.description: What to pass the program, one argument per element, applied verbatim. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

command.description: The program to run for this server. An absolute path, or a bare program name for PATH to answer. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

directory.description: An absolute path to start the program in. Left off, the directory crucible was started in. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

env.description: Environment variables for this server, applied verbatim — values, so nothing secret belongs here. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

envFrom.description: Environment variables for this server taken from crucible's own, keyed by the name the server reads and holding the name crucible reads — names, never secrets. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

handshakeSeconds.description: How long to wait for the server to agree a protocol version before giving up on it. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

requestSeconds.description: How long to wait for one request to this server before giving up on it. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

required.description: Whether a run that selected this server fails when it cannot be prepared, rather than carrying on without its tools. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

restarts.description: How many times this server may be started again after it ends. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

shutdownSeconds.description: How long the server is given to stop on its own before it is killed. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

servers.description: MCP servers that may be selected, keyed by the identifier their tools are qualified by. Nothing is started by being written here

color.description: Whether to write colour: auto follows the terminal and NO_COLOR, always and never override it

glyphs.description: Which characters crucible draws with: unicode for box drawing, ascii for a font that lacks it

syntaxTheme.description: Which theme fenced code is drawn in — a name from /theme, such as Monokai Extended, GitHub, Dracula or Nord

theme.description: Which colours crucible draws with: auto follows the terminal's own background, ansi spends only the sixteen it already has

toolDetail.description: How much of a tool call and its result one line shows

permissions.description: What runs without being put to you, what is refused outright, and where tools may reach

allow.description: Rules for calls that run without being put to you. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

ask.description: Rules for calls that are always put to you, whatever the mode says

deny.description: Rules for calls that are refused in every mode, beating any allow written beside them

extraDirectories.description: Absolute paths to directories outside the working directory that tools may reach. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

mode.description: What happens to a call no rule mentions: ask about every change and command, allow changes to files, or allow everything. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

promptCaching.description: Provider-side reuse of an identical prompt prefix, enabled through each provider's verified native mechanism by default

allowedMechanisms.description: Provider-neutral cache mechanisms still permitted after capability resolution; layers intersect this list

isolationScope.description: Broadest identity scope allowed to share a cache prefix

mode.description: Whether Crucible observes provider caching, prefers the verified native mechanism, requires it, or requires a documented opt-out

namespace.description: Bounded opaque user-owned label included in cache scope identity; never a provider cache key

persistentResources.description: Separate authority for remotely persisted cached-content resources

mode.description: Whether remote persistent cache resources are forbidden, reusable, creatable, or required; creation authority must come from user configuration

requestedRetention.description: Optional provider-neutral retention request under a hard duration ceiling

class.description: Provider-neutral retention class; extended retention must be chosen in the user configuration

maxSeconds.description: Hard maximum provider retention in seconds; required for ephemeral and extended retention

provider.description: Which provider to ask, by the name --model qualifies a model with. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory

apiKeyEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding this provider's API key — the name, never the key

baseUrl.description: Address to send this provider's requests to instead of the vendor's, for a gateway or a proxy

contextWindow.description: The context-window size in tokens, keyed by model name; an explicit value may opt into a larger native window

defaultContextWindow.description: The context-window size in tokens for any model of this provider not named above

effort.description: How hard to think before answering, when --effort does not say. Left off, the vendor's own default for whichever model is being asked

model.description: The model to ask when --model does not name one

providers.description: Per-provider defaults, keyed by provider name

sandbox.description: Operating-system confinement for commands and descendant processes

mode.description: Whether commands require verified kernel confinement, may use an explicit compatibility fallback, or run unconfined; only user configuration may weaken required

systemPrompt.description: What the model is asked under: how much it explains, and anything you would rather it were told instead

append.description: Instructions to add to crucible's own, said after them and every turn
examples: This repository is deployed on Fridays; never push to main.

custom.description: Instructions to ask every turn under in place of crucible's own, replacing them entirely. Read only from the configuration file in your home directory
examples: You are a reviewer. Read and explain; never edit a file.

tone.description: How much of the reasoning comes back with the answer: concise for the conclusion, explanatory for why it is that one, learning for what to know before touching the code again

updates.description: Whether crucible finds out that a newer release exists

check.description: Whether crucible asks GitHub which release is newest, and says so when this one is behind

title: crucible configuration
